title: Value of Entry Information for Sharp Survival Bounds under Dependent Left Truncation
banked_reason: Delivered tier incremental below novelty_target field: the arbitrary-support frontier remains an exponential optimal-face test, while the interpretable closed criterion is confined to three bins and the four-bin result is only a witness.
gap_reasons: The arbitrary-support information frontier is nevertheless an exponential optimal-face feasibility test derived from the projection theorem, while the interpretable closed criterion is confined to the staggered three-bin support and the four-bin result is only a witness.

The projected paper score is constrained by the deliberately discrete setup, absence of inference, censoring, calibration, or an applied demonstration, and limited practical guidance for supports of four or more cohorts.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the finite full-data and inclusion-only sharp polytopes, constructive survival/RMST and contrast bounds, an exact active-face information criterion, and the staggered three-bin phase result; correctness and the Ford–Fulkerson citation check passed. The field-tier claim collapsed because the arbitrary-support criterion remained an exponential optimal-face test and the interpretable theory did not extend beyond three bins except for a four-bin witness. A future re-raise must add substantial broad-support structure, inference/censoring/calibration, a concrete application, or a justified continuous-model bridge rather than more finite examples.
tldr: In a finite randomized survival study observed only after scheduled entry, when does the selected entry-by-failure table sharpen survival, RMST, and treatment-effect bounds beyond an inclusion-only analysis that already retains registry entry margins? The project develops exact full and coarsened cohort-capacity projections, an arbitrary-support active-face equality criterion, and a constructive closed criterion for staggered three-bin supports, with a proved uniform three-bin all-\(\Gamma\) phase proposition and a nonunique four-bin witness. It compares its finite inclusion-only envelope with the Peterson-form bound of Qian--Betensky; it does not identify the finite scheduled-support class with their continuous no-ties class.
gap: Dependent truncation leaves the failure margin unidentified, and existing sharp aggregate bounds do not say when selected entry labels add identifying value after registry entry margins and inclusion probabilities are already retained.
fill: It seeks exact constructive sharp sets, an equality/strictness frontier valid under nonunique coarse optima, a closed three-bin support theorem, sharp randomized-arm contrasts, an explicit independence limit, and a formally matched tightening of the Qian--Betensky Peterson envelope.
